sections.heading: UK immigration advice you can rely on
sections.text:
UK immigration rules change often, and a small mistake can mean a refused application, a lost fee and months of delay. We help families, workers, students and employers choose the right route, prepare complete evidence and submit applications that meet the current rules.

Every application is prepared and checked by advisers regulated by the Immigration Advice Authority (IAA). You can check our registration on the IAA's public register.

sections.heading: Which UK visa do you need?
sections.text:
The right visa depends on why you want to come to or stay in the UK:
- To join your husband, wife or partner: a spouse, partner or fiancé(e) visa
- To work for a UK employer: usually a Skilled Worker visa, sponsored by a licensed employer
- To study at a UK college or university: a Student visa, followed in many cases by the Graduate visa
- To visit family, friends or for business: a Visitor visa or, for many nationalities, an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA)
- To live in the UK permanently: Indefinite Leave to Remain, and later British citizenship

If you're not sure which applies to you, a consultation is the quickest way to find out.

sections.heading: UK immigration changes in 2026
sections.text:
Several important changes are under way. The government plans to move most routes to a 10-year "earned settlement" model for ILR, though the 5-year routes are still open for now. The Graduate visa drops from 2 years to 18 months for applications made from 1 January 2027. New Skilled Worker applicants have needed English at B2 level since January 2026.

We follow every change and will tell you how it affects your plans before you apply.
